thread:
olga: Quick note — I launched a tiny canary for nebula-ptq-int6 on onboarding traffic. Most looks normal but we're seeing two odd parse classes in streaming: (A) truncated JSON (unexpected EOF) and (B) JSON with a trailing comma before the final brace (parser: trailing comma).

tess: repro snippet from trace (streamed):
```
{"op":"log_event","payload":{"user":42,"msg":"payment failed", "ctx":{...}},
...<stream cut>
```
parser: unexpected EOF

ben: interesting — do we see trailing commas at the end or sometimes an extra comma followed by the closing chunk? could be a chunk boundary insertion bug. any correlation with sequence length or batch size?

chao: quick A/B: non-streaming nebula-int6 looks clean on a 500-sample replay. streaming shows ~3.1% fail for mid-long responses (200-600 tokens). float baseline <0.2%. int8 ~0.4%. so int6 path is the outlier.

telemetry-bot: canary-deploy nebula-ptq-int6 -> 2026-03-30T10:02:00Z (id: 98b3c2)

olga: hypotheses: (1) streamer is injecting a delimiter/comma when chunk concat happens (bad state machine handling of trailing delimiters), (2) kernel flush/evict on int6 path is dropping the final chunk and a partial token or comma remains.

tess: short-term mitigation ideas: enable an explicit end-sentinel (e.g., "\n\n<<END>>\n") in the streamer for canary only; enable a lightweight client json-healer that attempts safe repairs (strip trailing commas, append closing braces if balanced); log repaired_count separately so we don't hide regression.

ben: also propose a one-off internal retry: if parse fails and output_len > 120 tokens, retry once forcing sync-mode and mark metric repair_retry_win if successful. don't charge user quota for the canary retry.

chao: metrics to add: trailing_comma_count, truncated_json_count, repair_retry_win_rate, last_chunk_size_ms, final_chunk_presence_ratio. I'll wire them to the canary dashboard now.

olga: I'll flip end-sentinel for streaming canary and enable the healer as opt-in for canary traffic only. Running an eval harness to replay 10k real onboard prompts across float/int8/int6 for 1h; will compare structured-output pass, trailing-comma class, and latency impact.

tess: if the healer masks the bug too much, we should fail fast on >1% repaired_rate vs baseline and rollback. Keep repairs visible.

telemetry-bot: dashboard tile created: nebula-int6-canary-parse (metrics: trailing_comma_count, truncated_json_count, repair_retry_win_rate)

olga: plan recap: 1) enable end-sentinel for canary streaming (done), 2) enable client healer for canary, 3) allow single internal sync retry for long responses, 4) collect masked last-12-token snippets for failed parses for debug (PII scrubbed), 5) run 1h eval and report.

ben: if streaming-only confirmed, next step is narrow microquant rebuild looking at kernel flush order and streamer concat logic. add unit test for trailing delimiter handling.

chao: will watch infra eviction metrics too. tag @infra if preemptions increase.

olga: thanks all — keeping the canary small and observable. will post harness diffs in ~65m. :mag:
